nodes.content: Enable safe sim-to-real transfer for robotic peg insertion when friction and clearance changes are indistinguishable before contact.
requirements: Achieve ≥90% insertion success across held-out friction–clearance combinations using at most 20 real adaptation trials.
Keep peak contact force below 20 N during adaptation and deployment without privileged state observations.

nodes.content: Use wrench-guided microdithers to infer friction–clearance beliefs, then adapt impedance within 20 real trials using an 18 N predictive shield.
Can sub-18 N microdithers distinguish friction from clearance using wrist-wrench transients before the peg wedges?
Under 18 N, two-axis microdithers reveal clearance-dependent deadbands and friction-dependent wrench hysteresis, enabling ≥85% held-out regime identification before wedging.
Test shielded two-axis microdithers on 36 held-out simulated friction–clearance pairs; score pre-wedging identification accuracy from wrist-wrench traces and peak force.
Across 36 held-out simulated pairs, wrist-wrench microdithers identified 32/36 regimes before wedging; highest contact force was 17.2 N.
Advance shielded microdithers to a 20-trial real pilot; simulated identification reached 89% with 17.2 N peak force.
Pilot shielded wrench-conditioned impedance for 20 real adaptation trials; evaluate held-out insertions for ≥90% success and <20 N peaks.
Run 20 shielded real adaptation trials; test 60 held-out insertions across 12 friction–clearance pairs, logging success and peak force.
RealPilot-v1 dataset: 20 adaptation and 60 held-out insertion trials across 12 friction–clearance pairs, with wrist-wrench traces, outcomes, and peak forces.
Audit RealPilot-v1: compute held-out insertion success and adaptation/deployment peak forces; compare with 90% success and 20 N limits.
RealPilot-v1: 55/60 held-out insertions succeeded after 20 adaptation trials; peak force across all 80 trials was 19.1 N.
Release-phase wrench relaxation distinguishes high-friction, wide-clearance contacts from low-friction, tight-clearance contacts with ≥90% accuracy under 18 N.
Cross-validate release-decay classification on matched, sub-18 N RealPilot-v1 contacts; score high-friction/wide-clearance versus low-friction/tight-clearance accuracy.
On 24 sub-18 N RealPilot-v1 contacts, leave-pair-out release-decay classification reached 17/24 (71%), below the hypothesized 90%.
Which sub-18 N probe best resolves friction–clearance ambiguity when release-decay cues fail?
Compare lateral-frequency sweeps and torsional pulses in simulation using wrist-wrench-only regime identification under an 18 N shield.
Benchmark lateral-frequency sweeps against torsional pulses on 36 held-out simulated pairs; compare pre-wedging wrench-only identification and peak force.
ProbeBench-v1: 72 simulated probe traces across 36 held-out friction–clearance pairs, with regime labels, pre-wedging predictions, and peak forces.
Train distributionally robust compliant spiral search, calibrating wrench-triggered mode switches in 20 trials under an 18 N predictive shield.
Can wrist-wrench phase distinguish recoverable rim contact from incipient jamming across held-out friction–clearance pairs?
Wrist-wrench phase during compliant spirals predicts incipient jamming versus recoverable rim contact with ≥90% leave-pair-out accuracy below 18 N.
Using ProbeBench-v1 strata, calibrate shielded spiral switches in 20 real trials; measure phase-based rim/jam accuracy, held-out success, peak force.
After 20 calibration trials, leave-pair-out wrist-wrench phase classified 46/50 held-out rim/jam contacts correctly (92%); peak force was 17.6 N.
Retain microdither impedance as the primary policy; test phase-gated spiral recovery as a fallback before deployment.
Evaluate frozen phase-gated spiral fallback on held-out friction–clearance pairs, scoring rim/jam discrimination, insertion success, and peak force.
Run 60 held-out insertions per arm: frozen phase-gated fallback versus microdither-only; score rim/jam accuracy, success, and peak force.
FallbackBench-v1: 120 held-out insertion logs across frozen fallback and microdither-only arms, with rim/jam labels, outcomes, wrist-wrench traces, and peak forces.
Compare FallbackBench-v1 arm success and peak forces with RealPilot-v1; audit fallback rim/jam accuracy by held-out pair.
On FallbackBench-v1’s matched held-out pairs, fallback achieved 57/60 insertions (95%) versus microdither-only 52/60 (87%); peaks stayed ≤19.1 N.
Quantify phase-gated spiral switch latency, missed jams, and shield interventions from FallbackBench-v1 across held-out friction–clearance pairs.
FallbackBench-v1: phase switches lagged 140 ms, missing 3/5 jams on one high-friction/tight-clearance pair; only 2/5 insertions succeeded.
Defer phase-gated fallback deployment despite 95% aggregate success; first address 140 ms switch latency and high-friction/tight-clearance jams.
Freeze calibration; target <50 ms wrench-phase switches and retest held-out jam detection and insertion success under the 18 N shield.
Profile FallbackBench-v1 delays, implement 25 ms causal wrench-phase windows, and retest 60 new held-out insertions under an 18 N shield.
FallbackBench-v2 revises v1 with 25 ms causal phase-switch timestamps and 60 held-out retests, logging outcomes, jam labels, and forces.
Audit FallbackBench-v2 for phase-switch latency, jam recall, insertion success, and peak force; compare with v1 and deployment thresholds.
FallbackBench-v2 achieved 38 ms median switching but missed 4 jams; insertion success was 52/60 (87%), with 19.4 N peak force.
Reject phase-gated fallback for deployment: v1’s 95% masked pair-specific jams, while faster v2 achieved only 87% success.
Use wrench-conditioned jam-risk gating with 5-mm retract-realign recovery, calibrated within 20 trials under an 18 N predictive shield.
Can a 5-mm retract-realign maneuver avert high-friction/tight-clearance jams without adding force spikes or exhausting the trial budget?
Wrench-triggered 5-mm retract-realign recovers ≥4/5 high-friction/tight-clearance jams after ≤20 adaptation trials, with peak force <20 N.
Calibrate jam gating from ProbeBench-v1 strata in 20 real trials; test five held-out high-friction/tight-clearance jams for recovery and peak force.
After 20 real calibration trials, wrench-gated retract-realign recovered 4/5 held-out high-friction/tight-clearance jams; peak force was 18.7 N.
Advance retract-realign to broader held-out validation; 4/5 challenging jams recovered after 20 calibration trials without exceeding 20 N.
Freeze wrench-gated recovery after 20 calibration trials; validate held-out jam recovery, insertion success, and peak force across 12 friction–clearance pairs.
Using ProbeBench-v1 strata, test frozen retract-realign on 60 insertions across 12 held-out pairs; log successes, recoveries, and peak forces.
RetractBench-v1: 60 held-out insertion logs across 12 friction–clearance pairs, recording retract triggers, recovery outcomes, success, and peak force.
Audit RetractBench-v1 for success by friction–clearance pair, jam recovery, peak force, and ≤20-trial calibration compliance.
RetractBench-v1: 51/60 insertions succeeded (85%); seven false retracts caused five failures, while peak force stayed at 19.2 N.
Defer retract-realign deployment: it recovered 4/5 targeted jams, but false retracts cut held-out success to 85%.
Can sustained wrench evidence reduce false retracts without missing high-friction/tight-clearance jams under the 18 N shield?
Requiring 40 ms sustained wrench-risk evidence reduces false retracts to ≤2/60 while retaining ≥80% jam recall below 20 N.
Revise 40 ms sustained-risk gating using ProbeBench-v1 and RetractBench-v1; test 60 held-out insertions for false retracts, jam recall, success, force.
With 40 ms gating, false retracts fell to 2/60 and jam recall reached 8/10; success was 53/60, peak 19.3 N.
Defer deployment: microdithers scored 55/60 then 52/60; spirals missed jams despite 57/60; retracts rescued 4/5 but achieved only 53/60.
